name: MCP 2026-07-28 Spec — Stateless Core; MCP Tunnels; 3 New Extensions; 400M Monthly Downloads
hook: The biggest MCP protocol update since launch shipped July 28, 2026: the protocol drops its stateful session model for a stateless HTTP core — no initialization handshake, no Mcp-Session-Id, every request self-describing via _meta headers and routable via standard load balancers. MCP servers now deploy on serverless and edge infrastructure without a persistent connection. Three official extensions launch alongside: MCP Apps (server-rendered UI inside Claude), Tasks (async long-running operations), and Enterprise Managed Auth (IdP-based provisioning via Entra and Okta). MCP Tunnels (research preview) connect Claude to internal MCP servers behind a firewall with no inbound rules and no public endpoints. Beta SDKs in Python, TypeScript, Go, and C# are live now. MCP hit 400M monthly SDK downloads — 4× growth in 2026.

hook: Compresses tool outputs, logs, RAG chunks, and files before they reach the LLM: 92% token savings on 100-result code searches (17,765 → 1,408 tokens), 92% on SRE incident debugging (65,694 → 5,118 tokens), 73% on GitHub issue triage — accuracy held across GSM8K (0.870 baseline vs 0.870 compressed) and SQuAD v2 (97% accuracy at 19% compression). Ships as a Python library, HTTP proxy, and MCP server with three tools: headroom_compress, headroom_retrieve, headroom_stats. Claude Code integration is one command: `headroom wrap claude` launches a configured session. Trending today with 63.1K stars.
